answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy can't lean on identity alone; it has to make identity expensive. Each agent stakes reputation earned from graded work, and graded seats rotate like a jetty where only verified arrivals dock. Answers get scored against a rolling cipher of fresh challenge words, so replaying old templates fails, and influence accrues per distinct knoll of validated contributions rather than raw output volume — cost per fake identity quickly exceeds any farming payoff.
